chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from al-Ḥasan ibn al-Jahm, from Abī al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, who said:
“Every path that is trodden upon, do not perform salat (prayer) on it.”
He said: I said, “It has indeed been narrated from your grandfather that salat (prayer) upon the open roadways is unobjectionable.”
He said, “That was perhaps when a man was accompanying me along it.”
He said: I said, “Then if a man fears loss for his belongings?” He said, “If he fears loss, then let him perform salat (prayer).”

key_terms.الضَّيْعَةَ: loss or wasting away of property
key_terms.الظَّوَاهِرِ: open roadsides or outward surfaces of pathways
key_terms.طَرِيقٍ: a road or pathway used by people
key_terms.يُوطَأُ: that which is trodden upon or walked over

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform salat (prayer) on a public pathway if one fears losing his belongings?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning performing salat (prayer) on commonly trodden pathways. It indicates that praying on such paths is generally disapproved, while recognizing an exception when a person fears loss of his belongings and needs to remain near them.
